question: Compare approaches to memory in an AI support agent.
aliases: Compare memory approaches for an AI customer support agent
What are the approaches to memory in an AI support agent?

plan.objective: Compare the main ways an AI support agent can remember information within and across conversations.
plan.interpretation: Compare three memory approaches for a support agent (a conversation buffer with summaries, retrieval-based memory, and structured customer state) on what each keeps, how it fails, and what it costs, and cover privacy obligations that apply to all of them.
assumptions: The three approaches are the common building blocks; real systems often combine them.
"Memory" covers both the current conversation and information carried across conversations.

documents.title: Three kinds of memory for support agents
documents.snippet: A conversation buffer, retrieval-based memory, and structured customer state each keep different information.
documents.content:
Three kinds of memory for support agents

A conversation buffer keeps recent messages verbatim in the prompt, and a rolling summary replaces older turns with a shorter description. Retrieval-based memory stores past interactions or documents as embeddings and recalls the most similar items for each new message. Structured customer state stores specific fields, such as plan, open tickets, and stated preferences, that the agent reads and updates through tools.

Summaries can drop details that later turn out to matter, such as an order number mentioned early in the conversation. Similarity search can return memories that look related but are irrelevant or out of date.

documents.title: Designing memory for support agents
documents.snippet: Structured state is predictable and easy to audit; full conversation history grows token use with every turn.
documents.content:
Designing memory for support agents

Structured state is predictable and easy to audit, but it only captures the fields that someone decided to model.

Keeping the full conversation in the prompt is simple, but token use and latency grow with every turn. Retrieval adds an embedding call and a vector search before each response, but keeps the prompt size roughly constant. Reading a few structured fields adds little to the prompt and can be done with a single database lookup.

documents.title: Memory drift in long-running agents
documents.snippet: When an agent writes its own memories, mistaken inferences can be stored and repeated later.
documents.content:
Memory drift in long-running agents

When an agent writes its own memories, mistaken inferences can be stored and repeated in later conversations.

Combining approaches is common: a short buffer for the current conversation, structured state for account facts, and retrieval for past cases.

documents.title: Agent memory and personal data
documents.snippet: Stored conversation memory often contains personal data and needs a retention period and a deletion path.
documents.content:
Agent memory and personal data

Stored conversation memory often contains personal data, so it needs a retention period and a way to delete it on request.

Structured fields are easier to locate and delete than facts embedded in free-text summaries or vector stores.

short_answer.text: A conversation buffer with rolling summaries is the simplest approach, but token use and latency grow with every turn and summaries can drop details. Retrieval-based memory keeps the prompt size roughly constant but can return memories that are irrelevant or out of date. Structured customer state is predictable and easy to audit but only captures the fields someone decided to model. Systems commonly combine the three, and stored memory that contains personal data needs a retention period and a way to delete it.

findings.text: Structured customer state is easier to audit and delete than facts kept in summaries or vector stores.

limitations: The sources are practitioner guides; no controlled comparison of the approaches was found.
Cost and latency are described qualitatively and depend on the model and infrastructure used.
next_steps: List the facts your support agent must remember across conversations and decide which belong in structured fields.
Set a retention period and a deletion process before storing conversation memory.
